title: introduce-invocation-classifiers-and-stable-alert-bundles
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: alert noise from token-level percentiles has been causing paging fatigue — many incidents are duplicate symptom observations that differ only by invocation characteristics (sequence length, model variant, user tier). This PR introduces an explicit invocation-classifier layer that tags requests into a small, stable set of invocation classes at ingestion time and wires those classes into metric rollups, tracing sampling decisions, and alerting rules. Goals: reduce alert duplication, create stable SLO cohorts, and make latency/cost dashboards easier to reason about for oncall engineers.

What this PR does (summary):
- Adds invocation-classifier service that computes a deterministic class label using (model_family, approx_sequence_len_bucket, user_tier, content_type). The classifier is intentionally coarse (<= 12 classes) to keep cardinality low.
- Emits a new metric series prefix obs.invocation_class.* with per-class latency_histogram and token_cost_sum counters.
- Extends trace span enrichment to add invocation.class and ensures sampler uses class-aware reservoir sampling.
- Introduces alert bundle templates that map existing noisy SLO alerts to class-scoped versions; default behavior is to suppress cross-class deduplication noise.
- Provides console dashboards: Invocation Class Overview, Per-Class p50/p95/p99 latency and cost, and Class-Aware SLO Decomposition panels.
- Adds migration script (scripts/observability/migrate-alerts-to-classes.py) to convert 45 existing alert rules to class-aware bundles with a safe canary window.

Rollout plan:
1) Deploy classifier in beta on staging and dedicated canaries (1 day).
2) Start emitting obs.invocation_class.* metrics (no alerts) and collect two business days of baselines.
3) Migrate low-risk alerts (non-paging) to class bundles behind a feature flag (1–2 days).
4) Enable deduplicated paging behavior for high-noise alerts and monitor for missed pages for 72h.
5) Full rollout and feature flag removal in 2 weeks if no regression.

Backward compatibility & fallbacks: classifier emits invocation.class = "unknown" for older clients or if enrichment fails. Alert migration preserves original alert rule as a fallback and tags any suppressed event for manual review.

Related: Linear ENG-4321 handles the overall alert noise project; SUP-1024 is a customer-reported flood of duplicate latency pages. See design doc: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-4321/invocation-classifier-design (internal).

Checklist:
- [x] Classifier service implementation and unit tests
- [x] Metric export and Prometheus relabel rules for low-cardinality series
- [x] Trace enrichment + sampler wiring and integration tests
- [x] Dashboard JSON for console (importable)
- [x] Alert migration script and runbook update
- [x] Run perf microbenchmarks (no measurable 99th percentile regression on p99 tail for baseline workload)

Notes: this PR intentionally keeps classifier rules deterministic and static in code for the first rollout to avoid config churn; later iterations will move rules to a small config table with audit logs.

release_notes: Introduce invocation classifier to reduce alert duplication by grouping requests into stable, low-cardinality classes. Adds class-aware metrics, trace enrichment, and alert bundle templates. Rollout guarded by feature flags; no breaking changes expected.
notes_for_oncall: After rollout, oncall should: 1) check Invocation Class Overview dashboard for per-class volume; 2) verify dedupe false-positive rate by inspecting suppressed event log feed for the first 72 hours; 3) if missing pages are observed, disable observability.alerts.class_dedupe.enabled and open ENG-4321.
